program.name: Voice UX Lab
program.meeting_format: In person near Yangjae Citizen’s Forest Station; Google Meet online

weeks.title: Technology & team setup
weeks.deliverable: Notion workspace, GitHub repository, and development environment
activities: Read the Realtime API documentation. Do exercises with speech input and output.
Set up Notion, GitHub, and Codex

weeks.title: Voice-first UX & agent concepts
weeks.deliverable: Learning notes and initial voice interaction exercises
activities: Read about voice interfaces, tool calls, and prompt design.
Use these concepts in voice interaction exercises.

weeks.title: Project planning
weeks.deliverable: Project brief, user journey, interaction flow, architecture, and roles
activities: Select the user problem and project topic
Design the user journey and voice interaction flow
Select the architecture, roles, and development plan

weeks.title: Voice interaction prototype
activities: Use Codex for development. Keep the code in GitHub.
Make an interface for speech input and output.

weeks.title: AI agent & MVP
activities: Make the AI agent. Add the functions that it needs to call tools.
Write code for the tasks in the primary user scenario.

weeks.title: User testing & improvement
weeks.deliverable: Test findings, improvement list, and revised MVP
activities: Do user tests and collect feedback
Use the test results to decrease errors and response time.

weeks.title: Voice UX improvements
weeks.deliverable: MVP improvements and optional multimodal demo
activities: Use the test results to change the voice interface.
Add camera, display, or hardware support only if needed

weeks.title: Share results & prepare the demo
weeks.deliverable: Final code, technical docs, presentation, and demo
activities: Prepare the repository and technical documents
Make presentation materials and a demo
Hold the results meeting. Do a presentation rehearsal.

report.title: Executive summary
report.guidance: State the user problem and the project scope. Give the primary results and limitations.

report.title: Problem & research questions
report.guidance: Give the task, user needs, research questions, and success criteria.
paragraphs: The agent must identify the user’s task from speech. It must keep information from earlier turns in the conversation. It must use tools when the task needs them.
The team will examine voice as an interface between a user and an agent. In week 3, the team will select the user problem.

evidence.label: Published Voice UX Lab study brief

report.title: Agent & demo
report.guidance: Add links to the demo, source code, video, and setup instructions. List the tasks that the agent can do.

report.title: Design & architecture
report.guidance: Show the system design and the voice interface. Include tool calls, handoffs, and guardrails only if the project uses them. Give the reasons for design decisions.

report.title: Development & technical insights
report.guidance: State which development tasks used the API and Codex. Give each technical problem, its solution, and the checks of that solution.

report.title: Evaluation & improvement
report.guidance: Give the test method, scenarios, measures, results, failures, and improvements. Keep observations separate from conclusions.

report.title: Study records
report.guidance: Give each week’s work and the changes to the problem, design, and implementation.
paragraphs: The first two weeks cover the development tools and voice interface concepts. In week 3, the team will select the project.
In weeks 4 and 5, the team will make the prototype and agent. In weeks 6 and 7, it will do user tests and change the interface. In week 8, it will prepare the final presentation.
These activities are plans. This archive has no records of completed activities.

evidence.label: Published Voice UX Lab study brief

report.title: Individual work & reflections
report.guidance: Add each member’s approved name, role, work links, and comments. Keep meeting attendance separate from program completion.

report.title: Limitations & next steps
report.guidance: List the problems that remain and the limits of the tests. State which functions need more work.

report.title: Artifacts & references
report.guidance: Add the code, documents, presentation, demo video, approved photos, evidence index, and source links.
